title: What acme is
body: acme is the platform team's HTTP toolkit: an `App` with routes, options and middleware (`api/`), a problem-format error helper, generated platform limits, and a small CLI (`cmd/acme`). Standard library only; no third-party modules, ever.

title: How this toolkit adds an App option
body: To add an App option: 1) add the field, with a doc comment, to `Options` in `api/options.go` and apply it in `App.Handle` (`api/app.go`); 2) add its name to `AppOptions` in `api/options.go`; 3) add a row to the App options table in `docs/options.md`; 4) cover it with tests. The team suite checks 2 and 3 against the struct's fields.

title: How this toolkit adds a route option
body: Route options are fields of `RouteOptions`, passed to `app.Route(path, handler, opts)` and kept on `Route.Options`. To add one: add the field to `RouteOptions` in `api/options.go`, register the name in `RouteOptionNames`, add a row to the route options table in `docs/options.md`, and read it where the pipeline needs it (`App.Handle`).

title: Error responses the toolkit answers itself
body: Every error response the toolkit itself produces (limits, timeouts, rejected requests) goes through `api.Problem(status, title, detail, slug)` in `api/problem.go`, which answers `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457). Never answer `{"error": ...}` for these. Type slugs are kebab-case nouns, e.g. `request-deadline`.

title: Error catalogue review
body: New problem types are reviewed in the weekly API review; add the slug to the review doc before release. The review does not block merging.

title: Platform limits are generated
body: Platform limits live in `config/limits.json`. To add or change one, edit that file and run `go run ./scripts/genlimits`, which writes `api/limits_gen.go`. Never edit the generated file by hand; read values with `api.Limit(name)`.

title: Standard per-route rate limits are not decided
body: Standard per-route rate limits are NOT decided yet. Product owns them and has not chosen numbers. Do not invent limits; when work needs them, say so and ask.

title: Legacy v1 services
body: Old v1 services answer errors as `{"error": "..."}`. Kept only for those services; not for anything new in the toolkit.

title: Supported Go
body: Go 1.22 and newer, standard library only. `gofmt` clean; `go vet ./...` clean.

title: Release process
body: Releases are cut by the release manager from `CHANGELOG.md`. Version bumps are theirs; contributors never bump the version.

title: Middleware order
body: `app.Use(middleware)` runs middlewares in the order they were added, outermost first. Request logging stays last so it sees the final response.

title: Public API surface
body: Package `api` exports `App`, `New`, `Options`, `RouteOptions`, `Request`, `Response`, `Text`, `JSON`, `Problem`, `Limit` and `Logger`. Unexported names may change without notice.

title: Request logging
body: The toolkit logs through `api.Logger` (`api/log.go`), never `fmt.Print` to stdout. Warnings about requests go to that logger.

title: Handlers and responses
body: A `Handler` takes a `Request` and returns a `Response`. `Text()` and `JSON()` build the common shapes; set headers with `res.Set(name, value)`.

title: CLI errors are plain text
body: In `cmd/acme`, errors are one plain-text line on stderr, `acme: <message>`, with exit code 2. Never a panic or stack trace, never JSON, never the problem format: the CLI talks to a terminal, not to an API client.

title: CLI commands
body: `acme limits <name>` prints a platform limit; `acme version` prints the version. The CLI is built with `go build ./cmd/acme`.

title: Options tables
body: `docs/options.md` has one table for App options and one for route options. Columns: Option (in backticks, the struct field name), Type, Default, Description. One row per option; keep them in registration order.

title: Tests
body: Tests use the standard `testing` package only, in `api/*_test.go`, run with `go test ./api/...`. Test functions are named `Test<What>`.

title: The team suite
body: The platform team's suite lives in `teamtests/` and the platform CI runs it. It checks the option registries and `docs/options.md` against the structs' fields, and the generated limits against their source.

title: Scripts
body: `scripts/` holds maintenance tools run by hand: `go run ./scripts/genlimits` regenerates the limits file.
